title: Harvard Embryological Collection: public metadata as a serial-section crosswalk
research_problem: The Harvard Embryological Collection is a useful control for the Cole case because both are highly serial, but their seriality performs different work. HEC series reconstruct anatomical continuity inside one organism/specimen sequence; Cole issue numbers coordinate distributed publication units across subscribers.

collection_source.institution: Museum of Comparative Zoology, Harvard University
collection_source.description: Approximately 2,500 animal embryo series on approximately 30,000 microscope slides, created in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries by Charles Sedgwick Minot for embryological research.
documentary_apparatus: mostly original storage cabinets, now being replaced in conservation
collection_source.institutional_history: Non-human slides transferred from Harvard Medical School to MCZ in 1992; human embryo slides went to the National Museum of Health and Medicine. Since 2010 the collection has been inventoried/databased and cards/drawings linked to object records.

sample_records.research_use: Demonstrates that one current object record can preserve old HEC address, another historical number, physical series position, technique, preparator, publication citation and ledger documentation.

sample_records.condition_note: some blurred text, yellowing of adhesive
sample_records.research_use: Shows a current catalogue item representing multiple physical serial parts and retaining old address + publication + condition history.

critical_distinction_from_cole.HEC_seriality: section position orders parts through anatomical continuity; the sequence belongs to a prepared organism/embryo and a research collection
critical_distinction_from_cole.Cole_seriality: issue number synchronizes a distributed preparation with text/plate and subscriber time
critical_distinction_from_cole.publication_test: A numbered or serial slide collection is not automatically a material publication. Evidence of replicated/public distribution, issue/set architecture and recipient access is required before using 'publication'.

nineteenth_century_harvest_rule: Do not treat the whole HEC as nineteenth-century. Date-filter records before historical argument. The two public sample records above are early twentieth-century and are used here to establish the metadata/crosswalk mechanism, not as nineteenth-century evidence.
next_query: Filter MCZbase HEC records to preparation dates before 1900.
Select a small number of complete series with card scans/drawings and publication links.
Crosswalk technique terms against Minot's 1877 British-published technical discussion and microtome notice already present in the UK corpus.
Track recabinetting as a modern address transition while retaining the HEC number and linked card/drawing.
project_payoff: HEC demonstrates a successful modern strategy for preserving relation survival: the old identifier is not replaced by the new one; card, drawing, technique and publication metadata are attached to the current object record. This is the positive control against cases where glass survives but the historical crosswalk is lost.
